title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (rédaction n° 413, page A-18), filed upside down among the motives and Hodge notes. The closing joke ('au prochain rédacteur, au lecteur, au Pape ou au Général') is typical Bourbaki style. Section 7, 'Noyaux formels', sets up the formal analogue of a manifold germ, in a chart-based way.

Notation: K is a commutative ring and M a free K-module. P̂(M) is the completed algebra of polynomial functions on M, i.e. formal power series K[[M^∨]]. P̂_+(M;N) is the set of formal maps M→N without constant term. Such a g induces a substitution homomorphism g*: P̂(N)→P̂(M).

Def. 3 (formal chart). A formal chart of a K-algebra A is a pair (M, φ*), where φ*: P̂(M)→A is an algebra isomorphism. Two charts are compatible if they differ by formal maps in both directions, i.e. the transition automorphism is a substitution by a formal map with zero constant term.

Def. 4 (noyau formel). A noyau formel V is an algebra P̂(V) together with an equivalence class of formal charts. In modern terms this is a pointed formal smooth germ (Spf of a power series ring), with the formal coordinate changes fixed as the structure. Over a general base ring this genuinely restricts which algebra automorphisms count; over a field every local automorphism already qualifies.

Def. 5 (morphism). A morphism V→V' is an algebra homomorphism f*: P̂(V')→P̂(V) whose expression in any pair of charts is a substitution g* with g ∈ P̂_+(M;N). The text notes it suffices to check this for one pair of charts, and leaves the functorial properties and isomorphisms to the reader.

This is foundational material of the kind used for formal Lie groups in Bourbaki's Lie / Variétés drafts. It has no visible connection to the motives and Hodge-theory notes around it; the previous and next pages concern compatibility of topological and analytic Gysin maps with the (2πi)^p factor.
errors: Order of composition in Def. 3: ψ1 goes from M1 to M2, so ψ1* maps P̂(M2)→P̂(M1). The condition should then read φ2* = φ1*∘ψ1*, not ψ1*∘φ1*, unless a reversed composition convention is intended. The same applies to the second equation.
Def. 3 asks for maps in both directions, which is redundant: ψ2 is forced to be the formal inverse of ψ1. This is harmless.
Isomorphisms and the functoriality checks are explicitly left undone ('ce que nous laisserons faire...'). This is a deliberate omission in a draft, not a mathematical error.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Bourbaki draft page with foundational definitions of formal germs, misfiled among Grothendieck's motives notes. It contains nothing new and has no link to the surrounding Hodge/motives material.
transcription_corrections: The page image is upside down (rotated 180°). It is a typed Bourbaki rédaction (n° 413, page A-18), not a Grothendieck manuscript.

The transcription is otherwise essentially accurate. 'Soient V et V'' carries a handwritten underline. The hand-added marks near φ*^{-1} and the margin ticks are annotation strokes, not mathematical content.
